chunks: A Bedouin came to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and claimed against him seventy dirhams as the price of a she-camel he had sold to him. He said, “I have already paid you.” The Bedouin said, “Appoint between me and you a man who will judge between us.” Then a man from Quraysh came forward, and the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said, “Judge between us.” He said to the Bedouin, “What do you claim against the Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to him.” He said, “What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “I have paid him.” He said to the Bedouin, “What do you say?” He said, “He has not paid me.” He then said to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, “Do you have evidence that you have paid him?” He said, “No.” He said to the Bedouin, “Will you swear that you have not received your due and then take it?” He said, “Yes.” Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said, “I shall certainly seek judgment with this man before one who will judge between us by the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

So the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, came to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, with the Bedouin. ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said, “What is the matter, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “O Abū al-Ḥasan, judge between me and this Bedouin.” Then ʿAlī, peace be upon him, said, “O Bedouin, what do you claim against the Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to him.” He said, “What do you say, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “I have paid him its price.” He said, “O Bedouin, has the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, spoken the truth in what he said?” He said, “No, he has not paid me anything.” So ʿAlī, peace be upon him, drew his sword and struck his neck.

Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said, “Why did you do that, O ʿAlī?” He said, “O Messenger of Allah, we affirm your truthfulness regarding the command of Allah and His prohibition, and regarding Paradise and the Fire, reward and punishment, and the revelation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and should we not affirm your truthfulness concerning the price of this Bedouin’s she-camel? I killed him because he declared you false when I said to him, ‘Has the Messenger of Allah spoken the truth in what he said?’ and he said, ‘No, he has not paid me anything.’” Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said, “You were right, O ʿAlī, but do not return to the like of it.” Then he turned to the Qurashī, who had followed him, and said, “This is the judgment of Allah, not what you judged by.”

key_terms.أَعْرَابِيٌّ: a Bedouin claimant in the dispute
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: legal proof or evidence presented in judgment
key_terms.تَحْلِفُ: to swear an oath in support of a claim
key_terms.ثَمَنَ نَاقَةٍ: the price of a she-camel sold in the transaction
key_terms.حُكْمُ اللَّهِ: the ruling or judgment of Allah
key_terms.سَبْعِينَ دِرْهَمًا: seventy dirhams claimed as the sale price

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith portray Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام judging a dispute involving the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a dispute over the price of a she-camel brought before the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and then before Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام. It emphasizes absolute affirmation of the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and presents a dramatic narrative concerning judgment, truth, and the authority of divinely guided rule.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3425 - A Bedouin came to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and claimed seventy dirhams as the price of a she-camel he had sold to Him (sw).
The Prophet (sw) said: "I have paid you."
The Bedouin said: "Appoint someone between me and you who will judge between us."
Then, a man from Quraysh approached, and the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: "Judge between us."
The man asked the Bedouin: "What is your claim against the Messenger of Allah (swt)?"
He replied: "Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to Him (sw)."
The judge asked: "What do you say, O Messenger of Allah (swt)?"
The Prophet (sw) said: "I have paid him."
The judge then asked the Bedouin: "What do you say?"
The Bedouin replied: "He (sw) has not paid me."
The judge said to the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family: "Do you have any evidence that you have paid him?"
The Prophet (sw) said: "No."
The judge then said to the Bedouin: "Will you swear that you have not received your due and then take it?"
The Bedouin replied: "Yes."
Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: "I will indeed take this matter for judgment to a man who judges between us with the judgment of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic."

The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, went to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), accompanied by the Bedouin.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "What is the matter, O Messenger of Allah (swt)?"
He (sw) said: "O Abu al-Hasan (as), judge between me and this Bedouin."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "O Bedouin, what is your claim against the Messenger of Allah (swt)?"
The Bedouin replied: "Seventy dirhams, the price of a she-camel I sold to him (sw)."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) asked: "What do you say, O Messenger of Allah (swt)?"
The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: "I have paid him its price."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "O Bedouin, has the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, spoken the truth in what He (sw) said?"
The Bedouin replied: "No, He (sw) has not paid me anything."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), then drew his sword and struck his neck.

The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: "Why did you do that, O Ali (as)?"
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) replied: "O Messenger of Allah (swt), we believe you concerning Allah's (swt) commands and prohibitions, and regarding Paradise and Hell, reward and punishment, and the revelation of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic. Should we then not believe you concerning the price of this Bedouin's she-camel? I killed him because he denied you when I asked him, 'Has the Messenger of Allah (swt) spoken the truth in what he said?' and he replied: 'No, he has not paid me anything.'"
The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: "You have done right, O Ali (as), but do not repeat this again."
Then, He (sw) turned to the Qurayshi man who had followed him and said: "This is the judgment of Allah (swt), not what you had judged."
